summary: The delta (e705f22..7c72263) changes only 3 test files and fixes the major and both nits from review-e705f22. The major is fixed. OutboxMigrationIT now builds a static Pattern from the Java literal "\\b(ALTER|DROP|TRUNCATE)\\b", so the regex really is a word boundary on both sides. It uses Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE and no longer calls toUpperCase(). The redundant double case handling is gone, and SQL in any case is caught. additiveOnly passes the same Pattern object to AssertJ doesNotContainPattern(Pattern). The new test guardPatternBites passes the same constant three samples. It checks that 'DROP\nTABLE x' matches, that lowercase 'alter table y' matches, and that 'CREATE TABLE altered_things (id int)' does not match. So the guard cannot quietly go vacuous again, and the word boundaries are shown to stop false positives on substrings like 'altered'. This fits the engineer's report that a temporary 'DROP TABLE x' made the guard fail. Nit 1 is fixed: emptyPayloadsAreCorrupt now asserts last_error equals 'java.lang.IllegalStateException: Corrupt outbox payload'. Nit 2 is fixed: cancelledDuringBlockerCheckIsNotErased no longer asserts that runDue(...) returns zero, which removes the dependence on shared DB state. The status, profile, address and outbox assertions still prove the guard. Nothing else changed, and no production code was touched. V6 still passes the now-working guard, and I had already read it as only CREATE TABLE and CREATE INDEX statements. verify.md records forge-verify PASS with the user-service tests BUILD SUCCESSFUL, but the file does not name a SHA, so for AC-11 I am relying on the recorded output being for this head.
